{"self_assessment": "Impact: My most important contribution came at the start. I flagged that the original plan put the start at the tail, which the fall can't turn back from to feed the body. I proposed moving the start to the nose, with one line over the back and one under the belly, both flattening into the tail stem and then opening into the forks. The table adopted that design and rebuilt around it. A fish with a clear outline was a readable choice for the judge. I also took ownership of the lower tail fork and laid it so it would run on from the belly line.

Execution: I built my tail fork by tracing it from the pad, then stood dominoes back up and added links as the chain changed. I inspected the nose and tail areas repeatedly to find where the chain stopped. I found that the turn right after the start was too sharp, so I laid a gentle bridge into the top line and made a small fix at the start of that line. I kept to a plan and checked each stage before moving on.

Collaboration: I split the work clearly: Omar took the upper tail fork, I took the lower, Sofia the belly, and Jack the top line. I stayed off other people's areas so we didn't undo each other's work, and I shared what I found at the nose so the others could act on it. I kept the table focused on dry runs and join checks.

Leadership: I spoke up early with a clear, specific proposal when the plan had a structural problem, and I kept the table on the corrected design. In the last minutes I helped set who owned which join so hands weren't crowding the same spot. I was direct about what needed rethinking and offered a concrete fix each time.", "my_share_percent": 25}
